info.title: Kapto API
info.description: The local API of a Kapto collector: what it is doing, its episodes, recording control, and events as they happen.

get.summary:
The finalised episodes in the data directory, newest first. Folders
that aren't finalised, or whose summary can't be read, are left out.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: At most this many, newest first; 100 if not given.

parameters.name: accepted
parameters.description: Only those the quality checks accepted (`true`) or rejected (`false`), which leaves out those not checked yet; every episode if not given.

parameters.name: event
parameters.description: Only those with an event of this kind, e.g. `intervention`, which leaves out those whose events weren't read yet; every episode if not given.

500.description: The episode index can't be read

post.summary:
Stop recording and discard the episode: nothing of it is kept. Answers
once it is deleted.

400.description: The body isn't an abort request

post.summary:
Send an event. During an episode it is recorded in it; between episodes
it is only told to whoever watches. Either way every watcher is told.
Its kind must be one of `/api/event-kinds`.

400.description: The body isn't an event, or the event isn't well formed

409.description: Its kind isn't one that may be sent

post.summary: Start recording an episode. Answers once it is being recorded.

400.description: The body isn't a start request

409.description: An episode is already being recorded, a check of pre-flight's latest run failed, the profile is for another robot package, or the profile or task file can't be read

post.summary: Stop recording. Answers once the episode is finalised, and listed.

400.description: The body isn't a stop request

get.summary:
One finalised episode in full: its streams' counts, files, buffers, how
quickly it reached the disk, and the wall clock while it was recorded.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The episode's ID, as `/api/episodes` lists it.

400.description: The ID isn't an episode ID

404.description: No episode, here or deleted here, has this ID

get.summary:
When each frame of one of a finalised episode's cameras was received,
read from its recording by the recording's indexes: frame `n` is the
`n`-th. Needs no replay made.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The episode's ID, as `/api/episodes` lists it.

parameters.name: camera
parameters.description: The camera's stream, as the replay's opening lists it.

400.description: The ID isn't an episode ID

404.description: No finalised episode has this ID, or it has no such camera

500.description: Its recording can't be read by its indexes

get.summary:
Frame `n` of one of a finalised episode's cameras, as a picture the
browser draws: a compressed one as recorded, a raw one encoded as JPEG.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The episode's ID, as `/api/episodes` lists it.

parameters.name: camera
parameters.description: The camera's stream, as the replay's opening lists it.

parameters.name: n
parameters.description: The frame's number, from 0, as its frames list them.

200.description: The frame's picture, JPEG or PNG

400.description: The ID isn't an episode ID, or the number isn't a number

404.description: No finalised episode has this ID, or it has no such camera or frame

409.description: The frame can't be shown, and the message says why

500.description: Its recording can't be read by its indexes

get.summary:
What happened in one finalised episode: its events, in the order its
recording holds them, and the stretches it began but never ended. Before
the worker has read them, `read` is `false` and there are none.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The episode's ID, as `/api/episodes` lists it.

400.description: The ID isn't an episode ID

404.description: No episode, here or deleted here, has this ID

get.summary:
What the quality checks found on one finalised episode: whether it was
accepted, the settings it was checked with, and each check's result.
Before the worker has checked it, `accepted` is `null` and there are no
results.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The episode's ID, as `/api/episodes` lists it.

400.description: The ID isn't an episode ID

404.description: No episode, here or deleted here, has this ID

get.summary:
Where one finalised episode's replay is: not made, queued, being made,
ready with what it lacks, or failed with why. It asks for nothing:
`POST` does.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The episode's ID, as `/api/episodes` lists it.

400.description: The ID isn't an episode ID

404.description: No finalised episode has this ID

500.description: The job queue can't be read

post.summary:
Ask for one finalised episode's replay, its replay view to watch it
again in the web UI.
The worker makes it once, at low priority and not while an episode is
recorded: asking again while it is queued, being made or made changes
nothing; one that failed, or has since left the replay cache, is made
again. Answers where it is, `202` until it is ready.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The episode's ID, as `/api/episodes` lists it.

400.description: The ID isn't an episode ID, or the body isn't an empty object

404.description: No finalised episode has this ID

500.description: The job queue can't be read or written

get.summary:
One of the meshes of the robot a finalised episode was recorded with,
as plain triangles, from its replay: the binary form
`docs/reference/viewer-scene.md` specifies.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The episode's ID, as `/api/episodes` lists it.

parameters.name: n
parameters.description: The mesh's number, from 0, as the replay's scene's shapes give it.

400.description: The ID isn't an episode ID, or the number isn't a number

404.description: No finalised episode has this ID, its replay isn't made, or its scene has no such mesh

409.description: The mesh couldn't be read when the replay was made

500.description: Its replay view can't be read

get.summary:
What a finalised episode's replay shows, once
`/api/episodes/{id}/replay` says it is ready: its span, and the links
and values its stretches give, in their order, as the live stream's
opening message names them for the live view.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The episode's ID, as `/api/episodes` lists it.

400.description: The ID isn't an episode ID

404.description: No finalised episode has this ID, or its replay isn't made

500.description: Its replay view can't be read

get.summary:
The robot a finalised episode was recorded with, as `/api/robot/scene`
gives the one loaded now, once `/api/episodes/{id}/replay` says its
replay is ready: from the robot description its recording carries, so a
replay shows that robot whatever its package is now. Meshes are
numbered, each at `/api/episodes/{id}/replay/meshes/{n}`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The episode's ID, as `/api/episodes` lists it.

400.description: The ID isn't an episode ID

404.description: No finalised episode has this ID, its replay isn't made, or its recording carries no robot

500.description: Its replay view can't be read

get.summary:
A stretch of a finalised episode's replay, once
`/api/episodes/{id}/replay` says it is ready: the robot's newest pose
and each value's minimum and maximum in each of `points` equal parts of
it, read from the replay view at the coarsest step that still has that
many. In the binary form the viewer stream answers a look back with
(`KVHI`, the question's number 0), its span the episode's. Reading it
counts as opening the replay.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The episode's ID, as `/api/episodes` lists it.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Where the stretch begins, UTC nanoseconds.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Where it ends, UTC nanoseconds, included.

parameters.name: points
parameters.description: How many parts to merge it into: 1 to 10000.

400.description: The ID isn't an episode ID, or the stretch or points are missing, out of range or outside the episode

404.description: No finalised episode has this ID, or its replay isn't made

500.description: Its replay view can't be read

get.summary:
One finalised episode's statistics, worked out with its quality checks:
its duration, each stream's rate and loss, each joint's position, speed,
acceleration, jerk and effort (count, extremes, mean and percentiles),
each gripper's cycles. Before
the worker has checked it, `computed_utc_ns` is `null` and there are
none.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The episode's ID, as `/api/episodes` lists it.

400.description: The ID isn't an episode ID

404.description: No episode, here or deleted here, has this ID

get.summary:
One episode's uploads, where every object of it went, and whether it is
still stored here.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The episode's ID, as `/api/episodes` lists it.

400.description: The ID isn't an episode ID

404.description: No episode, here or deleted here, has this ID

post.summary:
Tries an episode's failed uploads again now, without waiting for
`upload.retry_failed_after`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The episode's ID, as `/api/episodes` lists it.

202.description: Queued: the upload lane takes them next

400.description: The ID isn't an episode ID

get.summary:
The kinds of events that may be sent: the vocabulary file's, or the
defaults without it, then each task's subtasks, and what is wrong with
the file. Read again on each request.

Events as they happen, over a WebSocket. Each message is one `Event` as
JSON. Connections from another site's web page are refused.

101.description: A WebSocket, on which each text message is one Event as JSON

403.description: The request came from another site's page

put.summary:
Save a layout as the default for the robot package Kapto runs, read by
every browser: written to `layouts/<package id>.toml` in the
configuration folder, checked as `layout.toml` is. Answers with it as
`/api/robot` now gives it, each panel with what the package lacks.

400.description: The body isn't a layout

409.description: The layout breaks a rule of layout.toml, or Kapto runs no robot package

delete.summary:
Remove the default layout saved for the robot package Kapto runs: the
live view is arranged by the package's own layout again, or the one
made from it. Answers with it.

post.summary:
Run pre-flight again: watch the streams for `capture.preflight_window`
and test the disk, then answer with each check's result. A run already
going is waited for rather than started again. Only between episodes:
its test file would compete with a recording's writes.

400.description: The body isn't a pre-flight request

get.summary:
Kapto's processes, the server first: whether each runs, since when, how
often it was started again, and its CPU, memory and threads. Answers even
while the capture process doesn't.

The profiles saved in the configuration folder, each marked available if
it records the robot package Kapto runs, and what is wrong with any that
can't be read. Read again on each request.

The robot and its streams as Kapto runs them: each joint with its limits
and the decoded value that drives it, each stream with its input, rate
and decoded fields, and problems that don't stop Kapto.

One of the scene's meshes as plain triangles, read from its file: the
binary form `docs/reference/viewer-scene.md` specifies.

parameters.name: n
parameters.description: The mesh's number, from 0, as the scene's shapes give it.

400.description: The number isn't a number

404.description: The scene has no such mesh

409.description: The mesh file can't be read

get.summary:
The robot as the web UI draws it: each link, in the order its poses are
sent as the robot moves, with its visual shapes, their colours and where
they sit. Meshes are numbered, each at `/api/robot/meshes/{n}`.

The settings Kapto runs with, each with its value and where it came
from. They are read when serve starts.

What Kapto is doing: the episode being recorded, each stream's counts,
and where the live view's stream is.

How much room the data directory has, and how much the episodes in it
take, including the one being recorded.

500.description: The file system's size can't be read

get.summary:
The tasks saved in the configuration folder, and what is wrong with any
that can't be read. Read again on each request.

Where uploads are: each destination's counts and every upload going or
failed.

500.description: The runtime state database can't be read

post.summary:
Tests a destination as an upload would use it, as `kapto upload check`
does: a small probe object written under its prefix, read back and
removed.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The destination's `name`, as `/api/uploads` lists it.

200.description: Written, read back and, if the credentials allow, removed

409.description: Its configuration or credentials can't be used

502.description: It couldn't be reached, refused the probe, or gave back another one

get.summary:
The versions of Kapto and of this API. The web UI checks it when it
loads.

AbortRequest.description: Stop recording and discard the episode; an empty object.

Aborted.description: The episode has been discarded: nothing of it was kept.

message.description: What happened: the code's summary and the specifics.

CameraFrames.description: A camera's frames in an episode.

times_utc_ns.description:
When each frame was received, UTC nanoseconds, in order: frame `n`
is the `n`-th.

CaptureStatus.description: What the capture process is doing.

episode.description: The episode being recorded, if one is.

oneOf.description:
Pre-flight's latest run, `null` until the first one, run when
capture starts, has ended. While an episode is recorded, the run it
keeps, with the checks its start waived.

seconds.description:
Seconds since the episode started, or since receiving started while
none is recorded.

streams.description: Each stream's counts over the same time.

values.description:
Each stream's newest decoded values, for the streams the live view
decoded any of. Sampled for display: not every message, and none
while nothing is decoded.

CheckRange.description: A span of an episode a check found something in.

end_utc_ns.description: Where it ends, the same way.

start_utc_ns.description: Where it starts, in UTC nanoseconds since the Unix epoch.

CheckResult.description: One check's result on an episode.

kind.description:
`gate` (deterministic; a failed one rejects the episode) or
`advisory` (only flags).

ranges.description: Where in the episode what it found is.

version.description: The check's version: results of different versions aren't alike.

ColumnInput.description: A column of a layout to be saved.

width.description: Its width relative to the other columns', from 1 to 12.

bytes_sent.description: The bytes sent of the episodes going up to it.

bytes_total.description: The bytes in all of those episodes.

failed.description: Episodes whose upload failed, tried again by themselves later.

throttled.description: How many requests it throttled, over every upload to it.

uploading.description: Episodes going up to it now.

DestinationStatus.description: How uploads to one destination are going.

DestinationTested.description: A destination tested with a probe object.

removed.description:
Whether it could be removed again; if not, it is still there: the
credentials may write but not delete, which uploads don't need.

took_ms.description: How long writing, reading back and removing it took, in milliseconds.

EpisodeBuffers.description: The ring buffers of an episode.

memory_bytes.description: The memory they took, in bytes.

peak_batches.description: The most batches waiting at once.

EpisodeClock.description: The wall clock while an episode was recorded.

max_uncertainty_ns.description: The largest uncertainty of a comparison, in nanoseconds.

samples.description: How often it was compared with the receive clock.

steps.description: How many times it jumped, e.g. when the time was set.

EpisodeDeletion.description: How an episode was deleted here.

deleted_utc_ns.description: When, in UTC nanoseconds since the Unix epoch.

destinations.description: Each destination holding a verified copy, by name.

buffers.description: The ring buffers between receiving and writing.

clock.description: The wall clock while it was recorded.

durability.description: How quickly what was received reached the disk.

ended_utc_ns.description: When it ended, in UTC nanoseconds since the Unix epoch.

files.description: The files in its folder, as its manifest lists them.

folder.description: Its folder, or where it was if it is no longer stored here.

id.description: Its ID, which is also its folder's name.

kapto_version.description: The Kapto version that recorded it.

oneOf.description:
The robot package it was recorded with; `null` if it is
`unchecked`.

The session profile it was recorded with, as it was then; `null` if
none was chosen.

How it was recovered, if recording stopped without finishing it;
`null` if recording finished it. A recovered episode's losses, buffers,
time to disk and clock aren't known: only finishing would have
counted them.

started_utc_ns.description: When recording started, in UTC nanoseconds since the Unix epoch.

stored_here.description:
Whether its folder is still here; `false` once deleted here, verified
elsewhere: what it says then is from the summary kept of it, and its
files are those uploaded (`/api/episodes/{id}/uploads`).

oneOf.description:
The task it was recorded for, as it was then; `null` if none was
chosen.

EpisodeDurability.description: How quickly an episode's messages reached the disk.

max_unsynced_ns.description: The longest any message waited, in nanoseconds.

p99_unsynced_ns.description:
99 % of the messages were on disk within this many nanoseconds of
arriving.

sync_interval_ns.description: How often the recording was synced, in nanoseconds.

events.description: Every event, in the order the recording holds them.

read.description:
Whether its events were read from its recording, which the worker
does after it is recorded; until then there are none.

unended.description:
Each beginning no later end of the same kind and ID closes: a
stretch still open when the recording ended, e.g. an intervention
whose end was never marked.

path.description: Its path inside the episode's folder.

EpisodePackage.description: The robot package an episode was recorded with.

hash.description:
Its content hash when recording started: episodes with the same hash
were recorded with exactly the same files.

EpisodeProfile.description: The session profile an episode was recorded with.

hash.description:
Its content hash: the same for every episode recorded with exactly
this profile, whatever its file is called.

mode.description:
How the robot was driven: `teleoperated`, `autonomous`, `mixed` or
`scripted`.

tags.description: Words to find the episode by.

EpisodeQuality.description: What the quality checks found on an episode.

accepted.description:
Whether it was accepted: no gate failed. `null` until it is checked,
which the worker does after it is recorded.

checks.description: Each check's result, in the order they ran.

computed_utc_ns.description:
When it was checked, in UTC nanoseconds since the Unix epoch; `null`
if not yet.

params_version.description:
The version of the quality settings it was checked with (the
`qa_params_version` of the `qa.toml` its recording carries); `null`
if it was checked with the defaults, or not yet.

EpisodeRecovered.description:
How an episode was recovered after recording stopped without finishing
it, by a crash, a kill or a power cut.

at_utc_ns.description: When it was recovered, in UTC nanoseconds since the Unix epoch.

bytes_cut.description:
Bytes cut off the end of its recording: written only in part, or not
on disk before recording stopped.

last_message_utc_ns.description: The newest message kept, in UTC nanoseconds; `null` if none was.

reason.description: Why it had to be recovered, in words.

EpisodeStatistics.description: An episode's statistics, worked out with its quality checks.

computed_utc_ns.description:
When they were worked out, in UTC nanoseconds since the Unix epoch;
`null` until the worker has checked the episode.

carried.description:
For a stream kept for late subscribers: how many messages kept from
before the episode it starts with, not counted in `received`.

decoded.description: Received messages whose live fields could be read.

disconnects.description: For a stream over a connection: how often the connection was lost.

loss_detection.description:
How messages lost before reaching Kapto were noticed: `sequence`
(exact, from sequence numbers), `rate_gap` (an estimate, from
silences) or `undetectable` (they can't be).

lost_upstream.description: Messages the source sent that never reached Kapto.

written.description: Received messages stored in the recording.

accepted.description:
Whether the quality checks accepted it: no gate failed. `null` until
the worker has checked it (`/api/episodes/{id}/qa` has the results).

ended_utc_ns.description: When recording ended, on the same clock.

events.description:
How many of its events are of each kind, by kind; `null` until the
worker has read them (`/api/episodes/{id}/events` has them).

id.description: Its ID, the same as its folder name.

kapto_version.description: The version of Kapto that recorded it.

mode.description:
How the robot was driven, as its profile said: `teleoperated`,
`autonomous`, `mixed` or `scripted`; `null` if not said.

oneOf.description:
The robot package it was recorded with; `null` if it is
`unchecked`.

profile.description: The ID of the session profile it was recorded with; `null` if none.

oneOf.description:
How it was recovered, if recording stopped without finishing it;
`null` if recording finished it. Its streams' losses aren't known.

started_utc_ns.description: When recording started, in nanoseconds since the Unix epoch.

stored_here.description:
Whether its folder is still here; `false` once deleted here, verified
elsewhere.

task.description: The ID of the task it was recorded for; `null` if none.

task_name.description: What people call that task; `null` if its file didn't say.

EpisodeTask.description: The task an episode was recorded for.

description.description: A sentence or two about it.

hash.description:
Its content hash: the same for every episode recorded for exactly
this task, whatever its file is called.

prompt.description: The instruction given to the operator or the policy.

objects.description: Every object of it there, once uploaded.

EpisodeUpload.description: An episode's upload to one destination, with every object of it there.

EpisodeUploads.description: One episode's uploads, and whether it is still stored here.

oneOf.description: How it was deleted here, if it was.

stored_here.description:
Whether its folder is here; `false` once deleted here, verified
elsewhere.

uploads.description: Its upload to each destination it was started for.

Event.description: Something that happened, sent as one JSON text message.

oneOf.description: For `capture_unreachable`: why, and what to do.

finalised.description:
For `episode_ended`: whether it was finalised; `false` if it was
aborted or failed.

EventKind.description: The kinds of event. More may be added: ignore an event of a kind you don't know.

EventPhase.description: Whether an event is a moment, one end of a stretch, or a whole one.

episode.description:
The episode it was recorded in; `null` if none was being recorded,
so it wasn't kept.

event.description: The event as it was kept.

EventVocabulary.description: Every kind of event that may be sent.

kinds.description:
The kinds: the vocabulary file's (or the defaults without it), then
each task's subtasks.

problems.description:
What is wrong with the vocabulary file; the defaults stand in for
its kinds while it has problems.

LayoutInput.description:
A layout as the page sends it to be saved: what [`ViewLayout`] gives,
without what the API works out.

LiveViewCounts.description: What became of a camera's frames on their way to the live view.

not_sent.description: Frames not sent because no viewer bridge was listening.

offered.description:
Frames offered: the camera's newest, at most `viewer.camera_max_fps`
a second.

skipped.description: Offered frames skipped because the live view held every slot.

superseded.description:
Frames replaced by newer ones before they could be sent: the
viewer bridge was slower than the camera.

PanelInput.description: A panel of a layout to be saved.

height.description: Its height relative to the other panels' in its column, from 1 to 12.

rotation.description: A unit quaternion: x, y, z, then w.

translation.description: x, y and z, in metres.

code.description:
The cause code the check fails with, which names it too, e.g.
`preflight.stream_silent`: what a start waives it by.

passed.description: Whether what was measured is enough.

remedy.description: What to do if it failed.

stream.description: The stream it is about, for a stream's check.

waived.description: Whether the episode being recorded was started despite its failure.

PreflightRequest.description: Run pre-flight again; an empty object.

PreflightRun.description: A pre-flight run: whether this machine can record what the robot sends.

checks.description:
Every check: the disk's room, its speed, then each stream in
declaration order.

passed.description:
Whether every check passed. While one failed, starting an episode is
refused (`capture.preflight_failed`) unless the start waives it, or
`capture.preflight` is `warn`.

ran_at.description: When it finished, in UTC, ISO 8601.

window_ms.description: How long the streams were watched, in milliseconds.

ProcessStatus.description: What one process is doing, as the API reports it.

cpu_cores.description:
CPU used over the last second, in cores: 1.0 is one core kept busy.
Unknown until it has been sampled twice, and off Linux.

last_exit.description: How it ended last, e.g. `signal: 9 (SIGKILL)`, if it ever did.

memory_bytes.description: Memory it holds (resident set), in bytes. Unknown off Linux.

name.description:
Its name: `serve` for the server itself, or the child's, such as
`capture` or `viz-bridge`.

pid.description: Its process ID while it runs.

restart_in_s.description: While it waits to be started again: the seconds left.

restarts.description:
How many times it ended on its own, or couldn't start, and was to be
started again.

uptime_s.description: Seconds since it was started, while it runs.

available.description:
Whether it can be used now: its package is the one Kapto runs. One
that isn't needs Kapto started with that package.

id.description: Its ID: its file's name without `.toml`.

mode.description:
How the robot is driven: `teleoperated`, `autonomous`, `mixed` or
`scripted`.

tags.description: Words to find its episodes by.

ProfilesOverview.description:
The saved profiles, and which can be used with the robot package Kapto
runs.

package.description: The robot package Kapto runs, if its streams belong to one.

problems.description: What is wrong with the profiles that couldn't be.

profiles.description: Every profile that could be read, by ID.

ReplayOpening.description:
What a replay shows, for the page to name what each stretch of it
holds, as the live stream's opening message does for the live view.

cameras.description:
The streams that are cameras, by name, in declaration order: their
frames come from `/api/episodes/{id}/cameras/{camera}/frames`. Empty
if the files the recording carries can't be read.

oneOf.description:
How the page arranges it: the layout the recording carries, or one
made from what it declares, each panel with what the recording
lacks; absent for a replay made before replays had one.

links.description: Each link's name, in the order a stretch gives its pose.

roles.description: Each role the recording's mapping gives a value.

start_utc_ns.description: When its first message was received, UTC nanoseconds.

streams.description: Each stream, by its number in a stretch, with its values.

ReplayRequest.description: Ask for an episode's replay; an empty object.

ReplayStatus.description: An episode's replay: whether it is made, and what it lacks.

bytes.description: Its size in bytes once ready.

lacks.description: What it lacks, and why, once ready: the robot, or some of its meshes.

values.description: Each decoded value, in the order a stretch gives their extremes.

ReplayValue.description: One decoded value of a replay's stream.

name.description: Its name: the field's, or `field[index]` for an array's.

plotted.description: Whether it is plotted; counters and clocks aren't.

count.description: How many values it holds: more than 1 for an array.

RobotFiles.description: The files a robot was loaded from.

mapping.description: Which decoded value drives which joint (`mapping.toml`).

effort.description: Its largest torque or force, in newton-metres or newtons, if known.

effort_from.description: The decoded value its effort comes from, if mapped.

lower.description: Its lowest value, in radians or metres, if limited.

mimics.description: The joint whose value it copies, if it does.

position_from.description:
The decoded value its position comes from, e.g.
`arm_joints.joint_positions[0]`, if mapped.

upper.description: Its highest value, in radians or metres, if limited.

velocity.description: Its largest speed, in radians or metres per second, if known.

velocity_from.description: The decoded value its velocity comes from, if mapped.

RobotOverview.description: The robot and its streams, as `kapto serve` loaded them.

files.description: The files it was loaded from.

joints.description: Its joints, in the order the description declares them.

layout.description: How the live view is arranged.

name.description: The robot's name in its description.

roles.description:
What each decoded value is for: every role the mapping gives a
field, written roles first, then each mapped joint's.

streams.description: The streams Kapto receives, in the order they are declared.

warnings.description:
Problems that don't stop Kapto, such as a mesh that isn't there or
a joint nothing drives.

RobotRole.description: A role and the decoded value that plays it.

field.description:
The value that plays it, e.g. `arm_joints.gripper` or
`arm_joints.joint_positions[0]`.

RobotScene.description: The robot as the page draws it.

links.description:
Every link, in the robot description's order: the order link poses
are sent in as the robot moves.

meshes.description:
How many mesh files the shapes use, each at
`/api/robot/meshes/{n}`, numbered from 0.

name.description: The robot's name in its description.

oneOf.description:
A sphere around everywhere the robot's shapes can be with its joints
moved within their limits, to frame the robot once and keep it in
view as it moves; absent for a robot with no shapes.

root.description: The link every other link hangs from, by its name.

decoder.description:
How its messages decode: `struct`, `json` or `msgpack`; none if they
are only recorded.

fields.description: The fields it decodes into, in order.

input.description:
Where it arrives, e.g. `udp 0.0.0.0:9000`, `tcp listen 0.0.0.0:9001`,
`tcp connect 192.168.1.20:9002` or `ros2 /joint_states`.

kept.description:
Whether its messages are kept for late subscribers (a ROS 2 topic
such as `/tf_static`): it may send them once and nothing after,
and every episode starts with the newest.

rate_hz.description: Messages per second the robot sends, if declared.

sequence.description:
Whether its messages carry a sequence number, so loss before Kapto
is counted exactly.

SceneLink.description: One link and what it looks like.

visuals.description:
Its visual shapes, in the order the description lists them. A mesh
that isn't there is left out; `/api/robot` warns of it.

SceneReach.description: A sphere in the root link's frame.

center.description: Its centre: x, y and z, in metres.

size.description: Its size along x, y and z, in metres.

oneOf.description: A cylinder along z with half-spheres on both ends.

length.description: The length of its cylindrical part, in metres.

scale.description: Scale along x, y and z, applied to the mesh's positions.

SceneShape.description: A shape, centred on its origin, any length along z.

SceneVisual.description: One visual shape on a link.

color.description:
Its colour: red, green, blue and alpha, from 0 to 1. A mesh part
with a colour of its own uses that instead.

origin.description: Where it sits in the link's frame.

SendEvent.description:
Send an event: something that happened now, or at a given moment, or
the beginning, end or whole of a stretch.

at_utc_ns.description:
When, in UTC nanoseconds; when capture takes it if not given. For a
whole stretch, when it began.

attributes.description: More about it, as names and texts.

id.description: Pairs a beginning with its end: required for both.

source.description: Who sends it: `api`, or `page` from the web UI; `api` if not given.

until_utc_ns.description: When a whole stretch ended; only for one.

SentEvent.description: An event as it was kept.

id.description: Pairs a beginning with its end.

phase.description: A moment, the beginning or end of a stretch, or a whole one.

default.description: Whether the value is the built-in default.

source.description:
Where the value came from: `default`, a file and line such as
`/config/kapto.toml:2`, an environment variable such as
`env KAPTO_SERVER_PORT`, or a flag such as `flag --port`.

value.description: Its value, as it would be written in `kapto.toml`.

file.description: The configuration file serve read, or would have read.

file_found.description:
Whether that file was there. Without it, every setting not given
otherwise has its default.

settings.description: Every setting, in the order the configuration reference lists them.

duration_s.description:
Stop by itself after this many seconds; without it, records until
stopped.

profile.description:
The ID of the session profile to record it with (`/api/profiles`):
it must be for the robot package Kapto runs. A copy of the profile
as it is now is kept in the episode.

task.description:
The ID of the task to record it for (`/api/tasks`). A copy of the
task as it is now is kept in the episode.

waive.description:
The codes of the failed pre-flight checks to record despite, e.g.
`preflight.stream_silent`: without them, a failed check of the
latest run refuses the start. The episode keeps the run, saying
which checks were waived.

StatisticSummary.description:
One statistic, summarised: a single value, or a distribution's count,
extremes, mean and percentiles.

count.description: How many values, for a distribution.

value.description: The value, for a single value.

viewer.description: Where the live view's stream is.

Storage.description: The data directory's room and use.

free_bytes.description: The bytes Kapto may still write there.

staging_bytes.description:
What episodes being recorded, or never finalised, take so far, in
bytes. It grows while an episode is recorded.

stop_below_bytes.description:
Below this many free bytes, an episode is finalised and none is
started (`capture.disk_stop_below`).

total_bytes.description: The size of the file system it is on, in bytes.

warn_below_bytes.description:
Below this many free bytes, Kapto warns the disk is running low
(`capture.disk_warn_below`).

oneOf.description:
For a camera, what became of its frames on their way to the live
view since capture started; absent for other streams.

lost_upstream.description: Messages the source sent that never arrived.

written.description: Messages written to the episode; zero while none is recorded.

age_ms.description: How long ago they were decoded, in milliseconds.

values.description:
The values, field after field and array elements in order, as
`/api/robot` lists the stream's fields.

description.description: A sentence or two about it.

id.description: Its ID: its file's name without `.toml`.

prompt.description: The instruction given to the operator or the policy.

problems.description: What is wrong with the tasks that couldn't be.

tasks.description: Every task that could be read, by ID.

UploadDestination.description:
A destination episodes are uploaded to, as `[[upload.destination]]`
names it.

url.description: Where it is, e.g. `s3://robot-data`; never its credentials.

UploadStatus.description: One episode's upload to one destination.

bytes_sent.description: The bytes of its files up so far.

bytes_total.description: The bytes of all its files.

failed_utc_ns.description: When it last failed, the same way.

failure_code.description: Why it failed last: its cause code.

failure_message.description: Why it failed last, in words.

key.description: The episode's key at the destination.

reported_utc_ns.description: When its progress was last reported, the same way; for throughput.

started_utc_ns.description: When it was first started, in UTC nanoseconds since the Unix epoch.

throttled.description: How many requests the destination throttled.

uploaded_utc_ns.description: When it was uploaded, the same way.

UploadedFile.description: One object of an uploaded episode.

path.description: Its path in the episode, e.g. `recording.mcap`.

sha256.description: Its SHA-256, as 64 lowercase hex digits.

UploadsOverview.description: Every destination's counts, and every upload not done yet.

destinations.description: Each destination, in the order the configuration lists them.

uploads.description: Each upload going or failed, newest first.

waiting.description: Episodes waiting for the upload lane, to every destination.

UploadsRetried.description: An episode's failed uploads, queued to be tried again.

Version.description: The versions of Kapto and of this API.

width.description: Its width relative to the other columns'.

ViewLayout.description:
How the live view or a replay is arranged: columns side by side, each a
stack of panels, as `docs/reference/package.md` describes `layout.toml`.

source.description:
Where it comes from: `package` (the package's `layout.toml`) or
`made` (made from what the package declares).

height.description: Its height relative to the other panels' in its column.

missing.description:
What it names that the package doesn't have, each a phrase; shown in
its place when not empty.

Viewer.description: Where the live view's stream is, on the host the API was reached on.

stream_port.description:
The port the robot's poses and plotted values are streamed on, as
they arrive, over a WebSocket (`docs/reference/viewer-stream.md`).

VocabularyKind.description: One kind of event that may be sent.

color.description: Its colour on the timeline, `#rrggbb`, if one is given.

description.description: When to send it, if said.

from.description:
Where it is defined: `file` (the vocabulary file), `default` (there
without one) or `task` (a task's subtask).

kind.description: The kind, as events carry it, e.g. `grasp` or `subtask.reach`.

stretch.description:
Whether it is usually a stretch, begun and ended, rather than a
moment.

task.description: For a subtask, the task's ID.
